newsitem.title: USA: NASD fines six firms for muni rule violations.
newsitem.headline: NASD fines six firms for muni rule violations.

text.p: The National Association of Securities Dealers said on Friday it fined six securities firms between $250 and $7,500 for violating political contribution reporting requirements of the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board's "pay-to-play" rule G-37.

NASD announced settlement agreements with Gruntal & Co Inc; Gates Capital Corp in New York; Minshall & Co Inc of Tulsa, Okla.; Chapman Securities Inc of Wichita, Kan.; Miller, Johnson & Kuehn Inc of Minneapolis; and Riedl & Co of Wichita, Kan.

The association also said that James Samford, a muni rep with Merchant Capital, agreed to pay $5,000 to settle charges that he failed to tell his firm that he contributed $17,500 to certain political action committees.
Those PACs contributed to the campaigns of "issuer officials," the settlement agreement says.

Gruntal & Co. agreed to pay $7,500, the largest of the fines, for failing to file quarterly reports under rule G-37 between July 1994 and June 1995. In that period, the firm participated in seven negotiated bond underwritings.

The Gates, Minshall, and Chapman firms agreed to pay $1,000 fines for G-37 reporting problems. The Miller firm agreed to pay $500, and the Riedl firm agreed to pay $250. All of the firms agreeing to settlements were censured.

In a statement, Minshall & Co said: "This violation was not a deliberate attempt to avoid reporting. We were under the incorrect assumption that we were only required to file (forms) if we participated in municipal underwritings."
The firm said it "never participated in a municipal underwriting and have no plans to do so in the future."
"During the entire year of 1995, we only did two municipal trades on an agency basis with total gross commissions of only $150," the firm said.
